production.note: US model years. Consumer Guide: "In 1987, Toyota added a new Supra Turbo model." (the A70 itself 'arrived in mid-1986' per Toyota, toyota-supra-history-2019). End: KBB and iSeeCars list a 1992 Supra Turbo (kbb-1992-supra-turbo), and Toyota's A80 was offered in the U.S. from 1993 (toyota-supra-history-2019). No opened page states in so many words that 1992 was the A70's last US model year.

body.note: 'coupe and new Sport Roof body styles, the latter with a lift-off roof panel'. The Sport Roof is a roof option on the liftback coupe, not a car sold under a Targa name.

configuration.note: 'DOHC 7M-GE 3.0-liter inline-six'; the Turbo used 'the new 7M-GTE turbocharged/intercooled version of the six'

displacementL.note: '3.0-liter inline-six'. No opened page gave the cc figure.

drivetrain.note: 'The Supra that arrived in mid-1986 remained rear-wheel drive on a new platform.'

transmission.note: Consumer Guide: "Transmission choices were five-speed manual or four-speed automatic"; for the 1987 Turbo, "Transmission choices remained the same".

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (one named-author article plus a database). 1989-1992 rating. Quote (Consumer Guide, Tom Appel, on the 1989 changes): "Horsepower was literally up a couple to 232, and torque was now set at 254 pound-feet." KBB 1992 Turbo Liftback 2D: "Horsepower: 232 @ 5600 RPM" (kbb-1992-supra-turbo). The 1987-1988 launch rating was 230 hp per Toyota: "the first Supra Turbo used the new 7M-GTE turbocharged/intercooled version of the six good for 230 hp and 246 lb-ft of torque" (toyota-supra-history-2019). 232 hp covers four of the six model years, so it is used.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (database; effectively one feed). 1991 Turbo hatchback (liftback); transmission not stated by iSeeCars. Quote (iSeeCars, 'Turbo 2dr Hatchback'): "Curb Weight | 3534 | lbs". iSeeCars 1992 prints the same (iseecars-1992-supra), and KBB's 1992 Turbo Liftback 2D (manual listed) prints "Curb Weight: 3534 lbs." (kbb-1992-supra-turbo); KBB and iSeeCars are likely one data feed, so the weight effectively rests on one database. 1991 is the earliest 232-hp year with a trim-specific figure: iSeeCars' 1989 page gives 3,459 lb for both the base and Turbo hatchbacks (iseecars-1989-supra), which does not look trim-specific. Toyota's history says the 1993 A80 Turbo, 'At 3,450 pounds, ... weighed about 125 less than its predecessor' (toyota-supra-history-2019), consistent but not a stated A70 figure.

sources.title: Toyota Supra: An Icon a Half-Century in the Making

provisionalNote: Power (232 hp, 1989-1992) rests on one named-author article (Consumer Guide, Tom Appel) and KBB (database); Toyota's own history gives only the 1987 launch rating (230 hp). Weight (3,534 lb, 1991 Turbo) rests on iSeeCars, with iSeeCars and KBB printing the same for 1992; these are likely one database feed, so it effectively rests on one database. A Toyota US press kit or brochure for 1989-1992, or a Car and Driver, Road & Track or MotorTrend specification panel for a 1989-1992 Supra Turbo, would replace both.
